data.one_liner: Rust-to-Dart bridge mimicking Flutter's platform channel via FFI without code generation.
data.what_it_does: Provides a platform-channel-like interface for bi-directional communication between Dart and Rust code. It uses Dart FFI to allow high-performance message passing with zero-copy binary transfers from Rust to Dart. It handles thread affinity, async calls, and Dart garbage collection finalizers without requiring code generators.
use_when: Building a Flutter application backed by custom Rust native code.
Seeking a platform-channel style API for Rust interop instead of manual low-level FFI bindings.
Transferring binary data between Rust and Dart where zero-copy or minimal-copy performance is critical.
avoid_when: Not using Rust in your project.
Needing web platform support (limited to native desktop and mobile platforms via FFI).
Projects that prefer automated Dart/Rust binding generation like flutter_rust_bridge.
strengths: Zero-copy transfers for binary data from Rust to Dart.
Familiar platform channel API on the Dart side.
No Dart code generation required to set up communication.
weaknesses: Requires manual Rust setup and companion Rust crate configuration.
Background thread channels require managing a custom RunLoop in Rust.
data.setup_notes: Requires compiling a companion Rust dynamic library (.so, .dll, or process) and setting up an FFI initialization function entry point.

alternatives.name: ffi
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick ffi when you want direct C-level foreign function bindings without platform-channel abstractions or Rust-specific crates.
